label: 2nd-3rd copy steps of long sequences (recall_idx 1-2, L>=8)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99% of mass), at the two steps right after the first output: recall_idx 1 (prev input <DEL>, 50% of mass) and recall_idx 2 (46%). It favors long sequences (L=9 holds 69% of mass, L=8 20%); short L fires rarely, apart from a small bump at L=3. Never fires in the original phase, and almost never at recall_idx 0 or 3 and later. Within that window, whether it fires depends on token content: inputs 1 and f (the first or second original token) fire about 4x more often and give the largest activations (top examples are ~0.9 of max on 1/f at recall_idx 1-2). No simple token set made the predicate much more precise. The timing predicate covers 87% of activation mass (dev) but has low precision (~0.15), because most long-sequence steps at recall_idx 1-2 stay inactive.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=12: 1, e, f, b; t=6: f, 1, q, n; t=14: 1, q, b, f) and the next token to output (most: a, i, v, o, c, n; least: h, g, -, b); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=3 & t=3, L=9 & t=11.
